 :Judgment:
This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Santhosh Hebbare @ Santhosh Hebbara in respect of the Road Traffic Accident dated 01.01.2023.

2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 01.01.2023 at about 2.15 p.m., when the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-S- SCCH 15 3 MVC No.1019/2023 5982 on the extreme left side on Tumkur - Bengaluru road, NH-48 service road, slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules and regulations and reached near Vishwashanthi Ashrama, Arishinakunte, at that time,
respondent's Ashok Leyland Dost Luggage vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-A-8357 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the Petitioner's motorcycle, resulting in the accident.
It is submitted that the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body due to the impact of the accident.

3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to Government hospital, Nelamangala and then he was shifted to ESI hospital, Rajajinagara and then shifted to Udhbhava hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.

Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-
with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
In pursuance of service of the notice issued to the Respondent No.1 and 2 they appeared through their Counsels and filed Objections to the claim petition.

The Respondent No.1 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
It is submitted by the respondent No.1 that the petitioner himself was tort feasor and the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of the petitioner.
It is submitted that the offending vehicle is insured under the respondent No.2.
It is submitted that the petitioner was not having valid driving license at time of the accident.
It is submitted that the amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, excessive, arbitrary, unreasonable and without any legal basis.

Hence, on Santhosh Hebbare Alias Santosh Hebbara vs Gopal M.P on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188506859/
2 these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

sentences.text:
The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
SCCH 15 5 MVC No.1019/2023
The respondent No.2 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending vehicle in favour of the respondent No.1.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.2 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The driver of the said vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the accident caused by rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license.
The age, avocation of the petitioner is denied.
The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. Vide order dated 31.08.2023 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road SCCH 15 6 MVC No.1019/2023 Traffic Accident that occurred on 01.01.2023 at about 2.15 p.m. on Bengaluru - Tumkur NH-48 Service Road, near Vishwashanthi Ashrama Gate, Arishinakunte,
Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Ashok Leyland Dost Lugguage vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-A-8357 by its driver?
2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3 ) What Order or Award?

6. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 17 and the Respondent No.2 has examined one witness as RW.1 and relied upon Ex.R1.
SCCH 15 7 MVC No.1019/2023 7.
Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order

sentences.text: Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Dost Lugguage vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-A-8357.
9.

In this regard the petitioner got himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on 01.01.2023 at about 2.15 p.m. when he was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-S-5982 on the extreme left side of Bengaluru - Tumkur service road and when it reached SCCH 15 8 MVC No.1019/2023 near Vishwashanthi Ashrama gate, Arishinakunte, the driver of the offending vehicle came from Nelamangala side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner's motorcycle resulting in the accident and injuries to the petitioner.
10.
The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 9 documents.
Ex.P1 is the FIR registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC and Sec.187 of IMV Act.
Said FIR is registered on the basis of the complaint given by one Abhishek on the date of the accident.
Hence, there is no delay in lodging the complaint.

Further Ex.P3 - spot mahazar discloses that the driver of the offending vehicle has come in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the motorcycle which is also substantiated by Ex.P5 - IMV report which shows that the front side of both vehicles has been damaged.
Ex . P6
shows that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries due to the impact of the SCCH 15 9 MVC No.1019/2023 accident.
Ex . P9 - charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and Sec.56 and 187 of IMV Act.
Hence these documents satisfactorily establish that accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

11. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by learned counsel for Respondent No.2 and in the cross-examination it is elicited that as on the date of the accident PW.1 was proceeding from Arishinakunte towards Nelamangala in his motorcycle.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence on the petitioner's side nothing much is elicited in the cross- examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of petitioner.
The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross-examination of Respondent No.2.
There is no material on record which SCCH 15 10 MVC No.1019/2023 suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding the cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also declined the suggestion imputing the cause of the accident to be due to his negligence.
The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.

The certified copies of FIR,
charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.

In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above Santhosh Hebbare Alias Santosh Hebbara vs Gopal M.P on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188506859/
4 accident.

sentences.text: In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of driver, driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
12. Issue No.2
: In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
13. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P6 wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner has sustained two grievous injuries to left compound fracture tibia middle 1/3rd left radius fracture, radius ulnar dislocation and produced Ex.P10 discharge summary of Udhbhava hospital and OPD slip of Employees State Insurance Corporation Medical college and model hospital and outpatient record of Nelamangala General hospital which discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment from 01.01.2023 to 14.01.2023 as an inpatient at Udhbhava hospital.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P3 medical bills.

As far as the medical bills are concerned PW.1 is cross- examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2, wherein he has deposed that he has taken treatment in ESI hospital and Udhbhava hospital and except suggesting that the petitioner has not incurred any medical expenses there is SCCH 15 12 MVC No.1019/2023 no evidence to disprove the medical bills produced by the petitioner.
Hence relying on the medical bills produced, petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.3,917/- under this head.
14. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and Ex.P6 discloses that the petitioner has sustained left compound fracture tibia middle 1/3rd left radius fracture, radius ulnar dislocation and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment as cause unbearable pain and he cannot walk or do any work as prior to the accident.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, trauma, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.30,000/- is SCCH 15 13 MVC No.1019/2023 awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:

In his evidence PW.1 has submitted he was aged about 35 years and he was working as a helper at Dhanalakshmi Enterprises and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. The medical records reflect that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries which has resulted in the disability and hence certainly he is unable to resume his work since the date of the accident.
It is submitted by the petitioner, he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
However in his cross-examination he has deposed that he has not produced any documents to show his income.

In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the Petitioner it would be proper to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the notional income as on the date of the accident, as per the guidelines of Lok-Adalat chart.
As per the relevant period the notional income is taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Taking into consideration that the petitioner due to the SCCH 15 14 MVC Santhosh Hebbare Alias Santosh Hebbara vs Gopal M.P on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188506859/
5 No.1019/2023 injuries might not have been in a position to work for at least 6 months.

16. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:
The petitioner has submitted that he has sustained permanent disability and in this regard adduced the evidence of - Orthopaedic Surgeon as PW.2.

PW.2 in his evidence has deposed that he has examined the petitioner on 14.02.2023 and assessed the disability as per the guidelines of "Guideline and Gazette notification issued by Ministry of Social justice and empowerment, Government of India".

He has submitted that the petitioner has stated difficulties in squatting, sitting cross legged,
climbing upstairs and walking on slope, kneel stand and pain in left leg and wrist.

PW.2 has submitted that the petitioner has permanent disability of 28% of left lower limb, 20% of left upper limbs, 19.5% of whole body and stated that the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.

PW.2 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2, wherein PW.2 admitted that he has not treated the petitioner and only assessed his disability and admitted that the waist foot movement is stable and the fracture is united and he has no problem in shoulder and elbow and there is no loss of movement.

The evidence of PW.2 discloses that the petitioner had sustained disability The evidence of PW.2 discloses that the petitioner had sustained physical disability at 28% of left lower limb, 20% of left upper limbs, if 1/3rd is taken it would be 16% to the whole body.
Accordingly, above mentioned disability can be read in evidence in terms of the observations made by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Bajaj Allianz Insurance Company Limited Vs Union of India.

the date of birth of the petitioner is 31.05.1988.
Going SCCH 15 16 MVC No.1019/2023 by the same, the age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e., 01.01.2023 was around 35 years.

Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. The loss of future earnings of petitioner due to his above injury and permanent physical disability comes to Rs.4,91,520/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 16 X 16%) and the same is awarded to him as compensation under this head.

sentences.text: Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that he might have to taken the help of an attendant.
Further, he would be requiring conveyance for movement.
His avocation has been hit due to his disablement.
He might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during his treatment.
Therefore, petitioner is granted Rs.20,000/- under this head.

20. TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid  96,000/-
up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  20,000/-
and conveyance 5. Medical expenses  3,917/-
 SCCH 15 18 MVC No.1019/2023 6. Loss of Future Income 4,91,520/-
 Total 6,61,437/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 6,61,437/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

21. Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest Santhosh Hebbare Alias Santosh Hebbara vs Gopal M.P on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188506859/
7 awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

22. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending SCCH 15 19 MVC No.1019/2023 vehicle.

As far as the liability is concerned respondent No.2 has got examined its senior legal manager as RW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that the insured vehicle (offending vehicle) was not having valid FC and RC to ply in the place of the accident.
Hence there is violation of MV Act and rules and there is breach of terms and conditions of the policy and hence respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
It is submitted that the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet under Sec.56 and 187 of IMV Act stating that offending vehicle did not have valid FC and RC as on the date of the accident.
23. In this regard learned counsel for the petitioner cross- examined RW.1 and it is admitted that the insurance policy was in force.
It is suggested that when the insurance policy was issued, the FC and RC is verified and the said suggestion is denied by RW.1.
Hence main contention taken by the insurance company is that they have to be absolved from the SCCH 15 20 MVC No.1019/2023 liability, since there is no valid FC and RC to the offending vehicle.

In this aspect the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has relied on the decisions laid down in MFA 1597/2011 (MV) dated 05.06.2013, between M/s The Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., vs C.N. Nagaraj &
others, wherein it has been observed that The insurance company having issued insurance policy in favour of IV respondent herein cannot contend that it had issued insurance policy, without verification of registration certificate and fitness certificate.

sentences.text: The insurance company is bound to ensure that a person to whom policy was issued is the registered owner of vehicle and insured vehicle is in a roadworthy condition.

If for any reasons, there is suppression of facts and misrepresentation of facts by insured, insurance company has to take steps to avoid the policy on the ground that it was obtained by non-disclosure of a material fact or by a representation of fact which was false in some material particular, as provided under sec.149(b) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (for short, the Act)
Therefore, this is not a valid ground for insurance company to avoid its liability against the 3rd party.

In MFA No.7864/2006 (MV), dated 23.08.2010,
between New India Assu. Co. Ltd., Vs Smt. S.
Vishalakshmi & another, wherein at para No.9 observed as follows:
"Under sec.41(7) of the motor vehicle act which contemplates that the registration is in force for a period of 15 years.

sentences.text: Thereafter, it was not renewed.
The insurance has taken a specific ground in written statement that after expiry for the registration the owner of the vehicle has not renewed the registration of the vehicle.
The owner has also not produced any evidence to show that the registration of the vehicle is renewed.

The accident was occurred on 20.04.2002 that is after 2 years from the date of expiry of the registration on the terms and conditions of the insurance that is on the date of the accident the vehicle in question was not registered or in the other sense there was no registration done.

Accordingly insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation."
24.
In the case on hand no doubt respondent No.1 appeared in this case and has not produced any documents to show that he had valid FC and RC as on the date of the accident.
However it has to seen as to whether the said breach is a fundamental breach which can absolve the insurance company from its liability.

In this regard if the decision relied SCCH 15 22 MVC No.1019/2023 by the counsel for respondent No 2 itself is taken into consideration it has been observed supra in MFA 1597/2011 (MV) dated 05.06.2013, between M/s The Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., vs C.N. Nagaraj &
others, wherein it has been observed that the insurance company having issued insurance policy in favour of IV respondent herein cannot contend that it had issued insurance policy, without verification of registration certificate and fitness certificate.

others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, this is not a valid ground for insurance company to avoid its liability against the 3rd party.
25. Hence the said observation is in favour of the respondent no 1 in this case though relied by respondent No2.
In the charge sheet it is only mentioned that there in no valid fitness certificate and there is no evidence adduced by respondent No 2 to show that there is no renewal of registration.

In addition in the cross examination of RW1 he has admitted that at the time of issuing insurance policy they verify the RC of the vehicle and hence they ought not to have issued policy without verifying the validity of the vehicle SCCH 15 23 MVC No.1019/2023 registration.

As far as no valid fitness certificate and non renewal of registration is concerned they are technical violations which cannot be considered as fundamental breach of policy conditions which can absolve the insurance company of its liability to pay compensation.
In addition the respondent No 2 has not adduced any evidence to show when the registration was lapsed and since how long it is not renewed.
Hence there is no cogent evidence to show non renewal of registration.

Hence respondent No 1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurance company are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and respondent no 2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the insured respondent and will have to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is "Partly in the Affirmative".
26. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hence these documents satisfactorily establish that accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR,
charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of driver, driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
12. Issue No.2
Accordingly, above mentioned disability can be read in evidence in terms of the observations made by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Bajaj Allianz Insurance Company Limited Vs Union of India.
Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
21. Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest Santhosh Hebbare Alias Santosh Hebbara vs Gopal M.P on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188506859/
7 awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.
Hence there is violation of MV Act and rules and there is breach of terms and conditions of the policy and hence respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
If for any reasons, there is suppression of facts and misrepresentation of facts by insured, insurance company has to take steps to avoid the policy on the ground that it was obtained by non-disclosure of a material fact or by a representation of fact which was false in some material particular, as provided under sec.149(b) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (for short, the Act)
Therefore, this is not a valid ground for insurance company to avoid its liability against the 3rd party.
However it has to seen as to whether the said breach is a fundamental breach which can absolve the insurance company from its liability.
In addition in the cross examination of RW1 he has admitted that at the time of issuing insurance policy they verify the RC of the vehicle and hence they ought not to have issued policy without verifying the validity of the vehicle SCCH 15 23 MVC No.1019/2023 registration.
As far as no valid fitness certificate and non renewal of registration is concerned they are technical violations which cannot be considered as fundamental breach of policy conditions which can absolve the insurance company of its liability to pay compensation.
In addition the respondent No 2 has not adduced any evidence to show when the registration was lapsed and since how long it is not renewed.
Hence there is no cogent evidence to show non renewal of registration.
Hence respondent No 1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurance company are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and respondent no 2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the insured respondent and will have to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
